answer: Data-grounded hypothesis: NLSY79 (12,686 respondents) के डेटा के अनुसार, जो respondents 1989 में अपनी savings में पैसा डाल रहे थे (present consumption के बजाय future के लिए saving करना = निम्न time preference / अधिक future-oriented व्यवहार), उनका 1989 BMI औसतन ~0.5 यूनिट कम था और obesity (BMI≥30) की odds लगभग 22% कम थी, sex, race/ethnicity, age, income, education, ASVAB और parental education को control करने के बाद (b = −0.49, p < 0.001; OR = 0.78, p = 0.017)। इसके विपरीत, जिनकी family net wealth 1985→1990 के बीच घटी (present-oriented व्यवहार का दूसरा proxy), उनका BMI थोड़ा अधिक था, लेकिन यह association controls के बाद सांख्यिकीय रूप से significant नहीं था (b = +0.12, p = 0.39)। इस प्रकार डेटा इस दिशा के अनुकूल है कि अधिक present-oriented time preference (जैसा कि saving behavior से मापा गया) अधिक BMI से जुड़ा है, परन्तु यह केवल एक associational hypothesis है — time preference का कोई direct measure डेटा में नहीं है, saving/wealth proxies liquidity constraints और परिपक्वता जैसे कारकों से confound होते हैं, और missingness/attrition non-random है (12,686 में से केवल 6,578 full-control model में बचे), इसलिए causal दावा नहीं किया जा सकता।

payload.hypothesis: In NLSY79, respondents who added to savings in 1989 (a proxy for lower time preference / more future-oriented behavior) had significantly lower BMI in 1989 (−0.49 BMI units, p<0.001) and lower odds of obesity (OR≈0.78, p=0.017) after adjusting for sex, race/ethnicity, age, income, education, ASVAB scores and parental education; the 1985→1990 net-wealth-trajectory proxy showed the same direction but was not significant. Equivalently, present-oriented behavior (drawing down savings or having none) is associated with higher BMI. Because time preference is not directly measured in the data, and saving/wealth proxies are confounded by liquidity constraints and life-cycle factors with substantial non-random attrition, this is an associational, data-grounded hypothesis, not a causal claim.
payload.workflow: Loaded data/nls_raw.csv (12,686×61). Converted 1981 height from feet-inches coding to inches (used 1985 height, fallback 1981, for 1989 BMI); treated weights as pounds (metadata 'kg' label implausible); excluded 11 weights >400 lbs and BMI outside 12–70; sentinel savings codes (9999996, 8192797) set to missing. Built proxies: (P1) 1989 savings behavior — put in vs took out (primary; categories 3/4 kept as separate groups, 1-vs-2 restricted sample as sensitivity), (P2) family net wealth trajectory 1985→1990 (grew vs declined; co-primary secondary). Outcomes: continuous BMI (primary, 1989) and obesity BMI≥30 (secondary logit); robustness with 1981 and 1992 BMI. Controls: sex, race/ethnicity, age, log family income, education, ASVAB average, parental education, family size. 10 regression models estimated with HC1 robust SEs; results in outputs/results.txt, code in outputs/analysis_bmi_timepref.py.
